solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suitor with style enthralling new society types

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the style word holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: An elegant admirer charms some fashionable newcomers in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' puts N inside MODE to make MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names fashionable high society, the smart set as a body of people.

clue.text: Wretch born on boat

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born in genealogies
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A miserable person was born aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boat' is a lighter, a cargo barge.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a contemptible or unfortunate fellow by this word, roughly 'wretch' or 'rotter'.

clue.text: Hostilities interrupting commercial settlement

indicators.note: interrupting means the hostilities word breaks into the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
war is open hostilities

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks off a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum granted by a tribunal or court to resolve a claim is a settlement.

clue.text: Man turning religious is butchered

indicators.note: turning means the man's name is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
sacred means religious or holy

explanation.surface: A man who turns to religion gets slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes MAS from SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter many people brutally is to butcher them.

clue.text: Showing audacity before match, one can get knotted

indicators.note: before places the audacity word ahead of the match

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or audacity
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Showing cheek ahead of a game, one gets told to get knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted' is British for 'get lost'; here literally. A cup tie is a knockout match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: This neckwear is tied in a knot at the collar, so it is something that gets knotted.

clue.text: Atelier designed for one who'd make a net profit?

definitions.text: one who'd make a net profit?

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are laid out to a new plan, rearranged

explanation.surface: A design studio is set up for someone who profits from fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges ATELIER. 'net' is the internet, not a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: An online retailer makes money on the internet, which is a net profit in a punning sense.

clue.text: Better class of religion found in Tyrrhenian location

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
RI is Religious Instruction, a school lesson in British schools

explanation.surface: A superior sort of faith is discovered somewhere in the Tyrrhenian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb, not an adjective. RI (Religious Instruction) is the old name for a religion lesson in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The island lies in the Tyrrhenian Sea in the Bay of Naples, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Ensure provision is made to do the dishes?

definitions.meaning: to supply what is needed, especially food
to provide the food dishes at an event, playfully read instead of washing up

explanation.surface: Make sure supplies are arranged so the washing up gets done.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies the dishes of food at a function, which is doing the dishes in another sense.

clue.text: Catch up with female working in temple

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the catch word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a trap is a catch
a hen is a female bird
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Catch up with a woman at work in a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TRAP to PART.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Doric temple of Athena on the Athenian Acropolis is the most famous temple of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Popular physicist short with a certain Gandhi

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: short means the physicist's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Paul Dirac was a British theoretical physicist

explanation.surface: A famous scientist falls short alongside a particular Gandhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims DIRAC to DIRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian prime minister was one of several notable Gandhis, so she is one particular Gandhi.

clue.text: Single mothers becoming learned theologians

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, hence single
mams is a homely word for mothers

explanation.surface: Lone mothers turn into scholarly experts on religion.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Muslim religious leaders and scholars, learned in Islamic law and theology.

clue.text: Hired privately, plotted to capture the monarch

indicators.note: capturing means the plotted word holds the monarch inside it

parts.note: to chart a course is to plot it on a map
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone schemed to seize the king, using hired private transport.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a crossword staple for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A chartered plane or boat is one rented for private use rather than a scheduled service.

clue.text: Main connection linking stars to conservation group

parts.note: Hydra is a large constellation, a group of stars
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A key link joins celebrities to an environmental charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is a water main, not 'chief'. The National Trust looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire plug is the outlet that lets firefighters tap a water main, so it connects to one.

clue.text: Cross appearing in church with Tempter going about?

indicators.note: going about means the tempter word goes round the church letters

parts.note: a lurer is one who entices or tempts

explanation.surface: An angry figure turns up in church while the Devil prowls around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' or a crucifix; it is a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: This dog is a crossbreed, typically greyhound with collie or terrier, so it is a cross.

clue.text: Perhaps Chuck senior has grizzle, eschewing hotel booze

parts.note: an elder is a senior person
Chuck Berry was the rock and roll pioneer, an example of someone with this surname

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the hotel letter is dropped from the grizzle word

parts.note: to grizzle is to whine or whimper
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A singer's father moans, avoiding the hotel, perhaps over drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eschewing' takes H out of WHINE to leave WINE. To grizzle is British for to whine fretfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink fermented from the dark fruit of the elder tree is a country homemade alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Consumes some chicken in trend towards recession?

parts.note: to down a drink is to consume it
a wing is one part of a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone eats a piece of chicken amid an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic downturn is a downward movement, a trend that leads to a slump.

clue.text: Mischievous, tailless cat, not accepted in stage show

indicators.note: tailless means the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip

indicators.note: not means the accepted letter is left out of the stage show

parts.note: a musical is a stage show
U is upper-class, socially accepted usage

explanation.surface: A cheeky Manx cat is refused a part in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts WHIP to WHI; 'not' drops U from MUSICAL to leave MSICAL. 'cat' is the whip, not a pet; U means socially acceptable in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfully fanciful or impish behaviour is mischievous in a light-hearted way.

clue.text: Satisfaction guaranteed with request

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: Customer contentment is promised along with any demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment or gratification is the feeling of being satisfied.

clue.text: I won't mean solid somehow, being shallow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the words are put together in some other way, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests they don't intend to be solid, which makes them seem superficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I WON'T MEAN SOLID; 'solid' tempts as a geometry hint, and in a way it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat character or argument lacks depth, figuratively having only length and breadth.

clue.text: Male dog slipping lead is more carefree

indicators.note: slipping its lead means the dog loses its first letter

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A male dog getting loose from its leash is happier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping lead' takes the first letter off TERRIER; 'lead' is the leash, but also the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jollier and more light-hearted is the comparative of a happy, cheerful mood.

clue.text: Literary work ends in tragedy, prompting curiosity

parts.note: a novel is a literary work

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A book ending sadly makes readers inquisitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A curiosity is a novel or unusual thing, a novelty item.

clue.text: Modern art medicine man exhibits

indicators.note: exhibits says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shaman puts on a display of contemporary artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is often called the modern art form, the youngest of the arts.

clue.text: Privileged member holding office, socialist is backed

parts.note: a party that is in holds office

indicators.note: backed means the socialist and is are read from back to front

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist

explanation.surface: A favoured member of a governing party turns out to be supporting a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns RED IS into SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within a group with access to privileged information is an insider.

clue.text: Strangely amusing nobleman lifted line

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the nobleman word is raised, reading upward

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An oddly funny aristocrat picked up a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses LORD to DROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry or quaintly comic humour is described as amusing in an odd way.

clue.text: Guts failing to save second artist

indicators.note: saving means keeping the second letter safely held within the failing word

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Lacking courage, someone fails to rescue another painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' as courage misleads; it means innards. RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts in the literal sense are the internal organs of the body, the viscera.

clue.text: Revolutionary wisdom gathered about new recruit

indicators.note: gathered about means the reversed wisdom goes round the new letter
revolutionary means the wisdom word is turned right round

parts.note: lore is traditional wisdom

explanation.surface: Radical learning is collected to take on a fresh member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns LORE into EROL, which 'gathered about' wraps round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up a new member or student is to enlist, which is what recruiting does.

clue.text: Change examination to accommodate current leader

parts.note: to edit text is to change it

indicators.note: accommodating means the examination word houses the current letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Revise the test to make room for the present head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' is a newspaper leader, not a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leading article stating the paper's opinion is called a leader.

clue.text: Greek island in which Corinthians curtailed amusement

parts.note: Cor is the short form for the biblical letters to the Corinthians

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the amusement word loses its last letter

parts.note: fun is amusement

explanation.surface: A Greek island where Corinth's people found their entertainment cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims FUN to FU.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ionian island off north-west Greece, also called Kerkyra, is one of the Greek islands.

clue.text: Investor for show one might be recording

definitions.meaning: a theatrical backer who puts money into a stage production
... Records was a well-known classical record label, so a recording might be on that label

explanation.surface: A financial backer of a production might be making a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Backers of stage shows are called this in theatre slang, and a famous EMI classical label bore the same heavenly name.

clue.text: Ely with Labour turning a shade Conservative?

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of the two words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cathedral city voting Labour starts to look Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges ELY LABOUR. Ely is an English cathedral city; the British Conservatives' colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep bright blue is a colour, and blue is the Conservative Party's colour, hence the question mark.
